## How the bits of a token are written

`encoding` has four strings of 6 octal digits: `w4` (bits 63-48), `w3` (47-32), `w2` (31-16) and `w1` (15-0). A token sets the bits that are 1 in its groups; the tokens of one instruction are ORed together.

### ROM bit flip

From the definitions, key `rom_bit_flip`.

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `applies_to` | ND-120 |
| `description` | ND-120 EPROM images have bits 22-27 inverted vs the assembled form |
| `mask` | 0x0FC00000 |
| `operation` | xor |
| `purpose` | When reading raw EPROM contents (e.g. from 45132L.bin + 45133L.bin), XOR with this mask to obtain the canonical assembled form used by the assembler and disassembler. When writing ROMs, apply the same XOR in reverse. |
